metadata.description: Burnout questionnaire family covering emotional exhaustion, depersonalization or cynicism, and professional efficacy.
metadata.intended_use: Occupational-health research and organizational assessment of burnout-related work experience.
metadata.development_history: Developed by Christina Maslach and colleagues with profession-specific versions.
metadata.measurement_rationale: Burnout is represented as a multidimensional work-related experience rather than a single distress score.
metadata.interpretation_notes: Use the correct MBI version and licensed scoring; burnout scores do not diagnose depression or a mental disorder.

versions.source_citation: Maslach Burnout Inventory; German commercial reference edition.

source_documents.title: Maslach Burnout Inventory official publisher reference
source_documents.license_name: Commercial test material; edition and use terms apply
source_documents.permission_basis: Only discovery and bibliographic metadata is stored. Item wording and forms are excluded until the exact German version and reuse terms are verified.

cosmin_metrics.internal_consistency: Cronbach's alpha ca. .90 (Emotional Exhaustion), .79 (Depersonalization/Cynicism), .71 (Personal/Professional Accomplishment) in der Originalnormierung.
cosmin_metrics.source: Maslach C, Jackson SE (1981). The measurement of experienced burnout. J Organ Behav, 2(2), 99-113.

versions.item_structure: 22 Items; Dimensionen: emotional exhaustion, depersonalization/cynicism, professional efficacy.
versions.scoring_notes: Exhaustion, Depersonalisation/Cynicism und Professional Efficacy werden getrennt nach MBI-Form ausgewertet.
versions.psychometric_summary: MBI ist die am häufigsten zitierte Burnout-Instrumentfamilie, aber kommerzielle Form und Subskalen müssen exakt angegeben werden.
